verses.zh: 唉！亚利伊勒，亚利伊勒，大卫安营的城，任凭你年上加年，节期照常周流。
verses.en: Ariel is as good as dead[NOTE:1]—Ariel, the town David besieged![NOTE:2] Keep observing your annual rituals;celebrate your festivals on schedule.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “Woe [to] Ariel.” The meaning of the name “Ariel” is uncertain. The name may mean “altar hearth” (see v. 2) or, if compound, “lion of God.” The name is used here as a title for Mount Zion/Jerusalem (see vv. 7-8).
Heb “the town where David camped.” The verb חָנָה (khanah, “camp”) probably has the nuance “lay siege to” here. See v. 3. Another option is to take the verb in the sense of “lived, settled.”

Heb “Add year to year; let your festivals occur in cycles.” This is probably a sarcastic exhortation to the people to keep up their religious rituals, which will not prevent the coming judgment. See J. N. Oswalt, Isaiah (NICOT), 1:527.

verses.zh: 我终必使亚利伊勒困难；她必悲伤哀号，我却仍以她为亚利伊勒。
verses.en: I will threaten Ariel,and she will mourn intenselyand become like an altar hearth[NOTE:1] before me.
notes: The term אֲרִיאֵל (ʾariʾel, “Ariel”) is the word translated “altar hearth” here. The point of the simile is not entirely clear. Perhaps the image likens Jerusalem’s coming crisis to a sacrificial fire.

verses.zh: 我必四围安营攻击你，屯兵围困你，筑垒攻击你。
verses.en: I will lay siege to you on all sides;[NOTE:1] I will besiege you with troops;[NOTE:2] I will raise siege works against you.
notes: The Hebrew text has כַדּוּר (khaddur, “like a circle”), i.e., “like an encircling wall.” Some emend this phrase to כְּדָוִד (kedavid, “like David”), which is supported by the LXX (see v. 1). However, the rendering in the LXX could have arisen from a confusion of the dalet (ד) and resh (ר).

The meaning of מֻצָּב (mutsav) is not certain. Because of the parallelism (note “siege works”), some translate “towers.” The noun is derived from נָצַב (natsav, “take one’s stand”) and may refer to the troops stationed outside the city to prevent entrance or departure.

verses.zh: 你必败落，从地中说话；你的言语必微细出于尘埃。你的声音必像那交鬼者的声音出于地；你的言语低低微微出于尘埃。
verses.en: You will fall; while lying on the ground[NOTE:1] you will speak;from the dust where you lie, your words will be heard.[NOTE:2] Your voice will sound like a spirit speaking from the underworld;[NOTE:3] from the dust you will chirp as if muttering an incantation.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “from the ground” (so NIV, NCV).
Heb “and from the dust your word will be low.”

Heb “and your voice will be like a ritual pit from the earth.” The Hebrew אוֹב (ʾov, “ritual pit”) refers to a pit used by a magician to conjure up underworld spirits. See the note on “incantations” in 8:19. Here the word is used metonymically for the voice that emerges from such a pit.
Heb “and from the dust your word will chirp.” The words “as if muttering an incantation” are supplied in the translation for clarification. See the parallelism and 8:19.

verses.zh: 你仇敌的群众，却要像细尘；强暴人的群众，也要像飞糠。这事必顷刻之间忽然临到。
verses.en: But the horde of invaders will be like fine dust,the horde of tyrants[NOTE:1] like chaff that is blown away.It will happen suddenly, in a flash.
notes: Or “violent men”; cf. NASB “the ruthless ones.”

verses.zh: 万军之耶和华必用雷轰、地震、大声、旋风、暴风，并吞灭的火焰，向她讨罪。
verses.en: Judgment will come from the Lord of Heaven’s Armies,[NOTE:1] accompanied by thunder, earthquake, and a loud noise,by a strong gale, a windstorm, and a consuming flame of fire.
notes: Heb “from the Lord of Heaven’s Armies [traditionally, “the Lord of hosts”] there will be visitation.” The third feminine singular passive verb form תִּפָּקֵד (tippaqed, “she/it will be visited”) is used here in an impersonal sense. See GKC 459 §144.b.

verses.zh: 那时，攻击亚利伊勒列国的群众，就是一切攻击亚利伊勒和她的保障，并使她困难的，必如梦景，如夜间的异象；
verses.en: It will be like a dream, a night vision.There will be a horde from all the nations that fight against Ariel,those who attack her and her stronghold and besiege her.

verses.zh: 又必像饥饿的人梦中吃饭，醒了仍觉腹空；或像口渴的人梦中喝水，醒了仍觉发昏，心里想喝。攻击锡安山列国的群众也必如此。
verses.en: It will be like a hungry man dreaming that he is eating,only to awaken and find that his stomach is empty.[NOTE:1] It will be like a thirsty man dreaming that he is drinking,only to awaken and find that he is still weak and his thirst unquenched.[NOTE:2] So it will be for the horde from all the nationsthat fight against Mount Zion.
notes: Or “that he [or “his appetite”] is unsatisfied.”
Or “that he is faint and that he [or “his appetite”] longs [for water].”

verses.zh: 你们等候惊奇吧！你们宴乐昏迷吧！他们醉了，却非因酒；他们东倒西歪，却非因浓酒。
verses.en: You will be shocked and amazed![NOTE:1] You are totally blind![NOTE:2] They are drunk, but not because of wine;they stagger,[NOTE:3] but not because of beer.
notes: The form הִתְמַהְמְהוּ (hitmahmehu) is a Hitpalpel imperative from מָהַהּ (mahah, “hesitate”). If it is retained, one might translate “halt and be amazed.” The translation assumes an emendation to הִתַּמְּהוּ (hittammehu), a Hitpael imperative from תָּמַה (tamah, “be amazed”). In this case, the text, like Hab 1:5, combines the Hitpael and Qal imperatival forms of תָּמַה (tamah). A literal translation might be “Shock yourselves and be shocked!” The repetition of sound draws attention to the statement. The imperatives here have the force of an emphatic assertion. On this use of the imperative in Hebrew, see GKC 324 §110.c and IBHS 572 §34.4c.

Heb “Blind yourselves and be blind!” The Hitpalpel and Qal imperatival forms of שָׁעַע (shaʿaʿ, “be blind”) are combined to draw attention to the statement. The imperatives have the force of an emphatic assertion.
Some prefer to emend the last two verbs from their perfect form to an imperative (e.g., NAB, NCV, NRSV), since the people are addressed in the immediately preceding and following contexts.

verses.zh: 因为耶和华将沉睡的灵浇灌你们，封闭你们的眼，蒙盖你们的头。你们的眼就是先知；你们的头就是先见。
verses.en: For the Lord has poured out on youa strong urge to sleep deeply.[NOTE:1] He has shut your eyes (you prophets),and covered your heads (you seers).
notes: Heb “a disposition [or “spirit”] of deep sleep.” Through this mixed metaphor (sleep is likened to a liquid which one pours and in turn symbolizes spiritual dullness) the prophet emphasizes that God himself has given the people over to their spiritual insensitivity as a form of judgment.

verses.zh: 所有的默示，你们看如封住的书卷，人将这书卷交给识字的，说：「请念吧！」他说：「我不能念，因为是封住了。」
verses.en: To you this entire prophetic revelation[NOTE:1] is like words in a sealed scroll. When they hand it to one who can read[NOTE:2] and say, “Read this,” he responds, “I can’t, because it is sealed.”
notes: Heb “vision” (so NASB, NIV, NRSV).
Heb “one who knows a/the scroll.”

verses.zh: 又将这书卷交给不识字的人，说：「请念吧！」他说：「我不识字。」
verses.en: Or when they hand the scroll to one who can’t read[NOTE:1] and say, “Read this,” he says, “I can’t read.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and if the scroll is handed to one who does not know a scroll.”
Heb “I do not know a scroll.”

verses.zh: 主说：因为这百姓亲近我，用嘴唇尊敬我，心却远离我；他们敬畏我，不过是领受人的吩咐。
verses.en: The Lord[NOTE:1] says,“These people say they are loyal to me;[NOTE:2] they say wonderful things about me,[NOTE:3] but they are not really loyal to me.[NOTE:4] Their worship consists of nothing but man-made ritual.[NOTE:5]
notes: The Hebrew term translated “Lord” here is אֲדֹנָי (ʾadonay).
Heb “Because these people draw near to me with their mouth.”
Heb “and with their lips they honor me.”
Heb “but their heart is far from me.” The heart is viewed here as the seat of the will, from which genuine loyalty derives.
Heb “their fear of me is a commandment of men that has been taught.”

verses.zh: 所以，我在这百姓中要行奇妙的事，就是奇妙又奇妙的事。他们智慧人的智慧必然消灭，聪明人的聪明必然隐藏。
verses.en: Therefore I will again do an amazing thing for these people—an absolutely extraordinary deed.[NOTE:1] Wise men will have nothing to say,the sages will have no explanations.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “Therefore I will again do something amazing with these people, an amazing deed, an amazing thing.” This probably refers to the amazing transformation predicted in vv. 17-24, which will follow the purifying judgment implied in vv. 15-16.
Heb “the wisdom of their wise ones will perish, the discernment of their discerning ones will keep hidden.”

verses.zh: 祸哉！那些向耶和华深藏谋略的，又在暗中行事，说：谁看见我们呢？谁知道我们呢？
verses.en: Those who try to hide their plans from the Lord are as good as dead,[NOTE:1] who do their work in secret and boast,[NOTE:2] “Who sees us? Who knows what we’re doing?”[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “Woe [to] those who deeply hide counsel from the Lord.” This probably alludes to political alliances made without seeking the Lord’s guidance. See 30:1-2 and 31:1.
Heb “and their works are in darkness, and they say.”
The rhetorical questions suggest the answer: “No one.” They are confident that their deeds are hidden from others, including God.

verses.zh: 你们把事颠倒了，岂可看窑匠如泥吗？被制作的物岂可论制作物的说：他没有制作我？或是被创造的物论造物的说：他没有聪明？
verses.en: Your thinking is perverse![NOTE:1] Should the potter be regarded as clay?[NOTE:2] Should the thing made say[NOTE:3] about its maker, “He didn’t make me”?Or should the pottery say about the potter, “He doesn’t understand”?
notes: Heb “your overturning.” The predicate is suppressed in this exclamation. The idea is, “O your perversity! How great it is!” See GKC 470 §147.c. The people “overturn” all logic by thinking their authority supersedes God’s.
The expected answer to this rhetorical question is: “Of course not.” On the interrogative use of אִם (ʾim), see BDB 50 s.v.
Heb “that the thing made should say.”

verses.zh: 黎巴嫩变为肥田，肥田看如树林，不是只有一点点时候吗？
verses.en: In just a very short time[NOTE:1] Lebanon will turn into an orchard,and the orchard will be considered a forest.[NOTE:2]
notes: The Hebrew text phrases this as a rhetorical question, “Is it not yet a little, a short [time]?”

The meaning of this verse is debated, but it seems to depict a reversal in fortunes. The mighty forest of Lebanon (symbolic of the proud and powerful; see 2:13; 10:34) will be changed into a common orchard, while the common orchard (symbolic of the oppressed and lowly) will grow into a great forest. See J. N. Oswalt, Isaiah (NICOT), 1:538.

verses.zh: 那时，聋子必听见这书上的话；瞎子的眼必从迷蒙黑暗中得以看见。
verses.en: At that time[NOTE:1] the deaf will be able to hear words read from a scroll,and the eyes of the blind will be able to see through deep darkness.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “In that day” (KJV).
Heb “and out of gloom and darkness the eyes of the blind will see.”sn Perhaps this depicts the spiritual transformation of the once spiritually insensitive nation (see vv. 10-12, cf. also 6:9-10).

verses.zh: 谦卑人必因耶和华增添欢喜；人间贫穷的必因以色列的圣者快乐。
verses.en: The downtrodden will again rejoice in the Lord;the poor among humankind will take delight[NOTE:1] in the Holy One of Israel.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “will rejoice” (NIV, NCV, NLT).
See the note on the phrase “the Holy One of Israel” in 1:4.

verses.zh: 因为，强暴人已归无有，亵慢人已经灭绝，一切找机会作孽的都被剪除。
verses.en: For tyrants will disappear,those who taunt will vanish,and all those who love to do wrong will be eliminated[NOTE:1]—
notes: Heb “and all the watchers of wrong will be cut off.”

verses.zh: 他们在争讼的事上定无罪的为有罪，为城门口责备人的设下网罗，用虚无的事屈枉义人。
verses.en: those who bear false testimony against a person,[NOTE:1] who entrap the one who arbitrates at the city gate[NOTE:2] and deprive the innocent of justice by making false charges.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “the ones who make a man a sinner with a word.” The Hiphil of חָטָא (khataʾ) here has a delocutive sense: “declare a man sinful/guilty.”
Legal disputes were resolved at the city gate, where the town elders met. See Amos 5:10.
Heb “and deprive by emptiness the innocent.”

verses.zh: 所以，救赎亚伯拉罕的耶和华论雅各家如此说：雅各必不再羞愧，面容也不致变色。
verses.en: So this is what the Lord, the one who delivered Abraham, has said to the family of Jacob:[NOTE:1] “Jacob will no longer be ashamed;their faces will no longer show their embarrassment.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “So this is what the Lord has said to the house of Jacob, the one who ransomed Abraham.” The relative pronoun must refer back to “the Lord.” It is uncertain to what event in Abraham’s experience this refers. Perhaps the name “Abraham” stands here by metonymy for his descendants through Jacob. If so, the Exodus is in view.
Heb “and his face will no longer be pale.”

verses.zh: 但他看见他的众子，就是我手的工作在他那里，他们必尊我的名为圣，必尊雅各的圣者为圣，必敬畏以色列的　神。
verses.en: For when they see their children,whom I will produce among them,[NOTE:1] they will honor[NOTE:2] my name.They will honor the Holy One of Jacob;[NOTE:3] they will respect[NOTE:4] the God of Israel.
notes: Heb “for when he sees his children, the work of my hands in his midst.”
Or “treat as holy” (also in the following line); NASB, NRSV “will sanctify.”
Holy One of Jacob is similar to the phrase “Holy One of Israel” common throughout Isaiah; see the at Isa 1:4.
Or “fear,” in the sense of “stand in awe of.”

verses.zh: 心中迷糊的必得明白；发怨言的必受训诲。
verses.en: Those who stray morally will gain understanding;[NOTE:1] those who complain will acquire insight.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and the ones who stray in spirit will know understanding.”
Heb “will learn instruction”; cf. NASB, NIV, NRSV, NLT “will accept instruction.”
